# magpie-mlx-serve

A [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) plugin that turns [mlx-serve](https://github.com/ddalcu/mlx-serve)'s
video models — MiniMax-H3, LTX-Video — into local `generate_video` videomakers.

magpie's gateway speaks the OpenAI videos API (`POST /v1/videos`) to any
provider whose model declares `capabilities.output.video`; mlx-serve instead
serves `POST /v1/video/generations` with base64 rgb8 frames + pcm_s16le audio
and leaves the muxing to the client. This plugin sits in the middle: it
translates magpie's video calls to mlx-serve, consumes the SSE progress
stream, and muxes frames + audio into an mp4 with ffmpeg.

```
magpie tool generate_video "a fox in snow" --model mlx-serve-video/<model id>
```

## Setup

```sh
brew install ffmpeg            # the muxer; skip if you have it
magpie plugin add magpie-mlx-serve
magpie plugin login mlx-serve-video    # no key needed — enter anything once
magpie plugin                        # mlx-serve-video, N video models
```

Every model in mlx-serve's `/v1/models` with `capabilities: ["video"]` is
listed automatically (`magpie provider models mlx-serve-video`).

The chat side of mlx-serve is already covered by magpie's built-in
`mlx-serve` preset — this plugin deliberately only serves the video models,
under its own provider id `mlx-serve-video`.

### Where mlx-serve is

`http://127.0.0.1:11234` by default. To point elsewhere:

```sh
magpie plugin options magpie-mlx-serve '{"url": "http://192.168.1.5:11234"}'
```

(or set `MLX_SERVE_URL` in magpie's environment; the option wins).

## Field mapping

| magpie (OpenAI videos)      | mlx-serve                              |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `prompt`                    | `prompt`                               |
| `seconds`                   | `num_frames` (× 24 fps; server snaps up the 17k+5 ladder) |
| `size` `1024x1024` / `16:9` | `width` / `height` (multiples of 32)   |
| `input_reference` (data URL) | `first_frame_image` (FL2VA packs)     |
| `last_frame` (data URL)     | `last_frame_image`                     |
| `reference_images`          | `ref_images` (REF2VA packs)            |
| `steps`, `seed`, `fast`, `turbo`, `chain_windows`, `negative_prompt`, `guidance_scale` | passed through |

Progress comes from mlx-serve's SSE stream; when a video isn't done within
magpie's ~20 s window the tool answers with an id and `generation_result`
picks it up, exactly as with any videomaker.

Measured on an M5 Max (128 GB), MiniMax-H3-FL2VA 8-bit, fast recipe, model
resident: 512×288 × 56 frames ≈ 30 s; 64×64 ≈ 15 s (mostly first-touch
paging of the 65 GB pack). Note 64×64 is far below the model's training
distribution — output there is abstract blobs; use ≥ 512 on the short side
for recognizable content.

## Limits

- Videos live in the plugin host's memory for an hour; a magpie restart
  drops in-flight jobs (finished ones are gone with it — download when made).
- One mux per video, on the Mac magpie runs on; ffmpeg is required.

## Test it without a 65 GB model

A mock mlx-serve for the whole path (models list, SSE generation, mux):

```sh
node scripts/mock.mjs &            # serves http://127.0.0.1:11299
magpie plugin options magpie-mlx-serve '{"url": "http://127.0.0.1:11299"}'
magpie tool generate_video "a fox" --model mlx-serve-video/mock-video --seconds 1 --size 64x64
magpie plugin options magpie-mlx-serve --reset 2>/dev/null || magpie plugin options magpie-mlx-serve '{"url": "http://127.0.0.1:11234"}'
```
